purpose: Close the same content-length bypass #4852 closed on the attachment route, on the two further routes a sweep of all 39 body-reading routes found. Of the seven that consult content-length, two use it as a boundary the same defeatable way: a chunked request carries no such header so Number(null || '0') is zero, and a malformed value gives NaN so Number.isFinite short-circuits. Both were proven by running them.
requiredInvariants: The two routes are not equally bad, and the record says so rather than flattening them. public-platform-assistant has no post-read body bound at all - MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH limits the message field, not the body - and requires no authentication. staff/[...path] does have a post-read check, so its limit holds; what fails is that it holds only after request.text() has already spent the memory. Reporting the second as an accepted-oversize defect would overstate it.
The staff route's malformed-header case was already handled by its author - it writes !Number.isFinite(...) and refuses - and that is left intact. Only the absent-header case is new.
The declared size stays as a cheap refusal for an honest client on both routes, and is no longer the boundary on either.

Reads are wrapped. A client disconnect rejects reader.read(); on the public route that would have become a 500 where the previous code gave 400, and on the staff route request.text() had no wrapper at all, so a disconnect was already an unhandled 500. The staff route gets a new REQUEST_BODY_UNREADABLE code because there was no prior mapping to preserve - unlike #4852, where an existing code covered it and reusing it was the minimal choice.

V5.2.1 is NOT claimed and its PASS from #4852 is untouched. Its text is about FILES; these routes accept JSON and a proxied body. No ASVS requirement covers raw body size on arbitrary routes - the nearest, V4.3.1 and V6.1.1, are about GraphQL/data-layer DoS and documenting rate limiting. This is an engineering defect with no requirement behind it, and filing it under a borrowed one would be the substitution this programme forbids. The ASVS decisions file is therefore not touched at all.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No migration, no new dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Found by sweeping all 39 body-reading routes under apps/web/app/api; 7 consult content-length and all 7 were examined. Two are false positives that delete the header while rebuilding a request, not size checks.
routeBodyBounds.spec.ts 4 of 4, all at route level.
Two mutations, each caught: reverting the public route to request.json() fails 1, and dropping the stream-failure wrapper alone fails 1.

A test bug of mine, corrected rather than worked around: the happy-path case first used a plain Request and failed inside the route at request.nextUrl. That failure actually proved the body had passed the bound and parsed - the crash was an unrelated missing NextRequest property. The test now builds a NextRequest.
